opening.text: Hi {name}. Your funding plan is ready. Ask about aid, forms or documents.
Hi {name}. {dream} decides admission without looking at your family's money, and for families earning under {threshold_income} it expects nothing from parents. Your plan is ready.

chips.q: What do my parents need to send?
chips.a: Their 2025 tax return, through IDOC, by {dream_aid_deadline}. {dream} accepts your own English translation, so you don't need to pay for one.

{dream}'s rule: for families earning under {threshold_income}, the expected parent contribution is zero. Your family's income is {band}. Your family pays the visa fees, {visa_fees} once. Still to confirm: {pending}.

The CSS Profile is the College Board's financial aid application. {dream} asks for it with code {css_code}, plus your parents' tax documents through IDOC. Regular Decision aid deadline: {dream_aid_deadline}.

opening.text: Hi {name}. {dream} gives international students merit scholarships only, so we count the full cost: about {net_per_year} a year on average. Your family could cover about {family_per_year}. The gap is about {gap_per_year} a year.

chips.q: How can I close the gap?
chips.a: Two routes can help. Start at {cc_name} and transfer to {dream}: {cc_gap_label}, {cc_gap_share} above what your family can pay. {transfer_note} Colleges that meet full need for international students: {strong_list}. Share an income range to see their estimates.

chips.q: How much do I show for the I-20?
chips.a: {dream} asks you to show {i20_amount} for the first year. {i20_note} This is what you show, not what you pay.
Colleges that give need-based aid to international students and meet full need: {strong_list}. Their price depends on your family's income, so share an income range to see an estimate.

opening.text: {name}, as a U.S. citizen you can file the FAFSA. {dream} has no published income rule, so there is no estimate yet. The official aid page has the next steps.
